title: Dynamic per-request KV quantization scheduler prototype
creator: Maya Chen
description: Prototype a dynamic, per-request scheduling layer that applies shard-level KV cache quantization under a request-specific fidelity budget. Goal: reduce GPU memory pressure during high-concurrency continuous-batching workloads while keeping downstream quality regressions within acceptable bounds. This ticket covers: design of the scheduler policy, offline calibration (per-head/per-layer quant tuning), integration into the runtime routing path, experiment harness for automated quality/regression checks, and rollout/rollback controls. The scheduler should support FP8, INT8, and INT4 codecs and be able to pick quantization levels on a per-KV-shard basis (not just model-wide). It must integrate with existing prefix/KV caching so that hot prefixes can be pinned to higher fidelity and cold prefixes aggressively quantized.
acceptance_criteria: Peak GPU KV resident memory reduced by >= 30% under target workload compared to baseline (no dynamic quant)
End-to-end LM quality drop (average log-prob delta) <= 0.25% for the production prompt set; 99th percentile quality regressions triaged and documented
99th percentile request latency remains within runtime SLO (+<10% overhead for scheduling decision)
Automated regression checks (prompt-set A/B harness) green for FP8 and INT8 modes; INT4 allowed only for targeted shards with documented risk
Fallback and rollback: when quality monitors detect sustained drift for >5 minutes, policy auto-reverts affected shards to last-good fidelity and emits alerts
experiment_steps: Design scheduler proto: inputs = request metadata (model, seq_len, routing tier), shard hotness score, recent quality delta; output = fidelity per shard
Implement offline calibration job to produce per-shard quantization lookup table (calibration dataset: production prompt set + synthetic long-tail)
Add stochastic rounding option to quant encode to reduce bias at INT8/INT4 levels
Integrate scheduler into runtime as a lightweight policy hook (C++ hot path + Python config), ensure decision cost < 250us median
Create evaluation harness: run 100k real-like requests on a dedicated test cluster measuring memory, latency, logprob, BLEU/ROUGE for downstream apps
Run controlled A/B on dedicated pool: baseline vs scheduler-enabled with FP8 default, collect metrics for one week
Iterate on shard-A/B: test shard pinning heuristics (top-k shards by access) and dynamic decay windows
metrics_summary: Initial runs (synthetic workload) show ~28-35% KV resident memory reduction when allowing FP8 on cold shards and INT8 on warm shards. Average log-prob delta observed: FP8 ~+0.07%, INT8 ~+0.12%, INT4 ~+0.9% on short sequences; INT4 degradation amplifies on long-context (>2048) requests. Scheduler decision overhead measured ~190us median on a p4d-like instance. Continuous batching improved amortized CPU cost per token by 6% when coupled with aggressive quantization.
initial_findings: FP8 offers the best quality/memory trade-off for most shards; calibration stable across seeds
INT8 acceptable for many intermediate layers but certain attention heads are sensitive and require per-head exceptions
INT4 produces large tail regressions on sequences with repeating patterns and for models with large head counts; use only for archival/cold shards
Per-shard adaptive policy (hotness + recency) outperforms global policies by ~12% in memory saved for same quality budget
Stochastic rounding reduced systematic bias for INT8 by ~0.03% log-prob on calibration set
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: silent quality regressions on long-tail prompts not covered by calibration dataset; Mitigation: broaden calibration set, add nightly drift detection and shadow evaluation
Risk: scheduler adds latency to hot path; Mitigation: cache decisions for identical request keys and compile decision graph to native code path
Risk: complicated rollback across dedicated pools; Mitigation: implement centralized rollback flag and per-pool override plus canary rollout
Risk: quantized KV incompatibility across model versions; Mitigation: include version tag in KV metadata and fallback to unquantized fetch if mismatch
next_steps: Finalize calibration dataset and run full sweep for 4 model families used in Hosted API
Open design doc for review: //confluence.redwood/kv-quant-scheduler (draft), invite runtime and research
Implement C++ hot-path prototype and micro-benchmark with realistic request traces
Prepare canary pool: enable FP8 default and monitor quality dashboards; schedule controlled rollout after 2 stable days
Coordinate with Console team to add per-request fidelity telemetry and new dashboard tiles
